summary: Phase 2 Warehouse Transfers tested end-to-end. Backend: 16/16 pytest cases PASS covering CRUD, status transitions (draft -> in_transit -> received), ship stock-decrement, receive UPSERT stock-increment, cancel/delete rules, validation (same wh, inactive wh, insufficient stock, empty items, auth), transfer_number uniqueness WT-YYYY-NNNN, filtering by status + warehouse_id, Phase 1 regression (warehouses list + _me/accessible), and Emergent object-storage upload+download via /api/products/upload-image + /api/files/{path}. Frontend: /admin/warehouses/transfers renders CorporateHeader, 'Переміщення між складами' title, status + warehouse filters, 'Нове переміщення' button; list shows 4 transfers with correct status pills (Чернетка/Прийнято/Скасовано). 'Переміщення' button on /admin/warehouses navigates correctly (data-testid='open-transfers-btn'). New transfer modal opens with from/to selects, note textarea, Створити чернетку button; product search area shows helper text until from-warehouse is selected (conditional rendering - correct UX). Transfer details modal opens on row click; action buttons correctly conditional on status: draft shows [Відвантажити, Скасувати, Видалити]; received/cancelled show no action buttons. End-to-end UI->API flow verified.

issues: Product search field (data-testid='product-search-input') is only rendered after from_warehouse is selected. This is correct UX but worth documenting - selectors depending on it must select from-warehouse first. Consider rendering a disabled input instead so the testid is stable.

critical_code_review_comments: warehouse_transfers.py: _generate_transfer_number uses COUNT(*)+1 within same year — if two concurrent POST happen in the same second they could get the same number (no DB uniqueness constraint enforcement visible in code). Recommend adding UNIQUE index on transfer_number + retry-on-duplicate loop. Not observed as a bug in practice (two sequential POSTs produced distinct numbers in test), but worth hardening.

ship_transfer: pre-flight stock check and decrement happen in separate statements — potential race condition if two ships execute concurrently. For MVP acceptable since this is admin-only, but note for future.
receive_transfer: UPSERT uses INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (correct, atomic).
List endpoint has no auth requirement (uses only db dep). GET is read-only so OK, but typically admin endpoints should be auth-protected for consistency.
WarehouseTransfersPage.jsx: 'eslint-disable' at top — would be nice to clean up actual lint issues instead.

data-testid coverage is good: new-transfer-btn, new-transfer-modal, from/to-warehouse-select, product-search-input (conditional), save-transfer-btn, transfer-row-{id}, transfer-details-modal, ship-transfer-btn, cancel-transfer-action-btn, delete-transfer-btn, open-transfers-btn, filter-status-select, filter-warehouse-select all verified.
seed_data_creation: During the test run, several draft transfers were created and cleaned up. WT-2026-0001 (received, pre-existing from manual smoke test), WT-2026-0002 (cancelled by test_cancel_draft), WT-2026-0003 (received by test_full_ship_receive_flow) remain in DB. All drafts created with items of product_id=74 qty=1-2 on UA->PL2. UA stock on product 74 was decremented by 1 (receive flow) + 1 (full flow) = ~2 units; PL2 UPSERT added corresponding qty. Resulting stock drift is minimal and reversible; recommend DB cleanup if desired.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 2 Warehouse Transfers is fully functional. Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_warehouse_transfers_phase2.py covers all critical paths. Phase 1 regression (warehouses CRUD, _me/accessible) and object-storage upload/download also included. PL2 (id=3) is now active - do not re-activate.
